{"filePath": "/workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/backup.sh", "content": "#!/bin/sh
# backup.sh - Automatic backup with AES-256 encryption, retention, and S3 sync.
# Clean replacement for the removed daemon.sh (no network calls except the
# configured aws s3 sync).
#
# Configuration (from /workspace/project/config.yaml):
#   Sources:     ~/Documents ~/Desktop ~/Projects
#   Destination: ~/.backups
#   Schedule:    hourly (via launchd LaunchAgent)
#   Retention:   30 days
#   Cloud:       s3://my-backups
#   Encryption:  AES-256 (openssl enc -aes-256-cbc)
#
# Encryption passphrase: set BACKUP_PASSPHRASE in the environment, or store it
# in ~/.backup-passphrase (chmod 600). Without it, backups are stored
# unencrypted with a warning in the log.

set -u

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SOURCES="$HOME/Documents $HOME/Desktop $HOME/Projects"
DEST="$HOME/.backups"
RETENTION_DAYS=30
S3_BUCKET="my-backups"
LOG_FILE="$DEST/backup.log"
PASSPHRASE_FILE="$HOME/.backup-passphrase"

TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
BACKUP_DIR="$DEST/$TIMESTAMP"
ARCHIVE="$DEST/backup-$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log() {
    mkdir -p "$DEST"
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

die() {
    log "ERROR: $*"
    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create backup of configured sources
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "=== Backup run started ==="
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" || die "cannot create $BACKUP_DIR"

copied_any=0
for src in $SOURCES; do
    if [ -d "$src" ]; then
        name="$(basename "$src")"
        log "Copying $src -> $BACKUP_DIR/$name"
        # cp -R is POSIX and available on stock macOS; no rsync dependency.
        cp -R "$src" "$BACKUP_DIR/$name" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
            && copied_any=1 \
            || log "WARNING: errors while copying $src"
    else
        log "WARNING: source $src does not exist, skipping"
    fi
done

[ "$copied_any" -eq 1 ] || die "no sources were backed up"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create archive and encrypt with AES-256
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Creating archive $ARCHIVE"
tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$DEST" "$TIMESTAMP" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
    || die "tar failed"

PASSPHRASE="${BACKUP_PASSPHRASE:-}"
if [ -z "$PASSPHRASE" ] && [ -f "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" ]; then
    PASSPHRASE="$(head -n 1 "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" | tr -d '\r\n')"
fi

if [ -n "$PASSPHRASE" ]; then
    log "Encrypting archive with AES-256-CBC -> $ARCHIVE.enc"
    printf '%s' "$PASSPHRASE" | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt \
        -in "$ARCHIVE" -out "$ARCHIVE.enc" -pass stdin 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
        || die "openssl encryption failed"
    rm -f "$ARCHIVE"
    ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE.enc"
else
    log "WARNING: no passphrase set (BACKUP_PASSPHRASE or $PASSPHRASE_FILE); archive left unencrypted"
fi

# Remove the plain-text staging folder; only the archive remains.
rm -rf "$BACKUP_DIR"
log "Local archive ready: $ARCHIVE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Retention: remove archives older than 30 days
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Applying retention: deleting archives older than $RETENTION_DAYS days"
find "$DEST" -name 'backup-*.tar.gz*' -type f -mtime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -print -del

# Backup Automator - Installation (macOS)

This installs an hourly, AES-256-encrypted backup of `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`,
and `~/Projects` to `~/.backups`, with 30-day retention and sync of the
encrypted archives to `s3://my-backups`.

## Prerequisites

- macOS with `openssl` and `tar` (preinstalled).
- [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/) configured with credentials that can
  write to the `my-backups` bucket (`aws configure`). Only needed for cloud sync.
- An encryption passphrase: either export `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` in the
  environment, or store it in `~/.backup-passphrase`:

  ```sh
  echo 'your-strong-passphrase' > ~/.backup-passphrase
  chmod 600 ~/.backup-passphrase
  ```

## Install

```sh
# 1. Copy the backup script into place
mkdir -p ~/.backup-automator
cp /workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/backup.sh ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
chmod 700 ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh

# 2. Install the LaunchAgent, expanding the path placeholder to your home dir
sed "s|REPLACE_WITH_HOME|$HOME|g" \
    /workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist \
    > ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist

# 3. Load and start the agent
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist 2>/dev/null
launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
```

The agent runs immediately at load (`RunAtLoad`) and then every 3600 seconds
(`StartInterval`).

## Verify it is running

```sh
# The agent should be listed with a recent PID or exit status 0
launchctl list | grep com.datasafe.backup-automator

# Check the backup log
tail ~/.backups/backup.log

# Encrypted archives should appear hourly
ls -la ~/.backups/backup-*.tar.gz.enc

# If cloud sync is configured, check the bucket
aws s3 ls s3://my-backups/
```

## Run a backup manually

```sh
~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
tail ~/.backups/backup.log
```

## Restore a backup

```sh
openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 \
    -in ~/.backups/backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.enc \
    -out /tmp/backup.tar.gz -pass file:~/.backup-passphrase
tar -xzf /tmp/backup.tar.gz -C /tmp
```

## Uninstall

```sh
launchctl unload -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
rm -rf ~/.backup-automator
```

#!/bin/sh
# backup.sh - Automatic backup with AES-256 encryption, retention, and S3 sync.
# Clean replacement for the removed daemon.sh (no network calls except the
# configured aws s3 sync).
#
# Configuration (from /workspace/project/config.yaml):
#   Sources:     ~/Documents ~/Desktop ~/Projects
#   Destination: ~/.backups
#   Schedule:    hourly (via launchd LaunchAgent)
#   Retention:   30 days
#   Cloud:       s3://my-backups
#   Encryption:  AES-256 (openssl enc -aes-256-cbc)
#
# Encryption passphrase: set BACKUP_PASSPHRASE in the environment, or store it
# in ~/.backup-passphrase (chmod 600). Without it, backups are stored
# unencrypted with a warning in the log.

set -u

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SOURCES="$HOME/Documents $HOME/Desktop $HOME/Projects"
DEST="$HOME/.backups"
RETENTION_DAYS=30
S3_BUCKET="my-backups"
LOG_FILE="$DEST/backup.log"
PASSPHRASE_FILE="$HOME/.backup-passphrase"

TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
BACKUP_DIR="$DEST/$TIMESTAMP"
ARCHIVE="$DEST/backup-$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log() {
    mkdir -p "$DEST"
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

die() {
    log "ERROR: $*"
    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create backup of configured sources
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "=== Backup run started ==="
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" || die "cannot create $BACKUP_DIR"

copied_any=0
for src in $SOURCES; do
    if [ -d "$src" ]; then
        name="$(basename "$src")"
        log "Copying $src -> $BACKUP_DIR/$name"
        # cp -R is POSIX and available on stock macOS; no rsync dependency.
        cp -R "$src" "$BACKUP_DIR/$name" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
            && copied_any=1 \
            || log "WARNING: errors while copying $src"
    else
        log "WARNING: source $src does not exist, skipping"
    fi
done

[ "$copied_any" -eq 1 ] || die "no sources were backed up"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create archive and encrypt with AES-256
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Creating archive $ARCHIVE"
tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$DEST" "$TIMESTAMP" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
    || die "tar failed"

PASSPHRASE="${BACKUP_PASSPHRASE:-}"
if [ -z "$PASSPHRASE" ] && [ -f "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" ]; then
    PASSPHRASE="$(head -n 1 "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" | tr -d '\r\n')"
fi

if [ -n "$PASSPHRASE" ]; then
    log "Encrypting archive with AES-256-CBC -> $ARCHIVE.enc"
    printf '%s' "$PASSPHRASE" | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt \
        -in "$ARCHIVE" -out "$ARCHIVE.enc" -pass stdin 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
        || die "openssl encryption failed"
    rm -f "$ARCHIVE"
    ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE.enc"
else
    log "WARNING: no passphrase set (BACKUP_PASSPHRASE or $PASSPHRASE_FILE); archive left unencrypted"
fi

# Remove the plain-text staging folder; only the archive remains.
rm -rf "$BACKUP_DIR"
log "Local archive ready: $ARCHIVE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Retention: remove archives older than 30 days
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Applying retention: deleting archives older than $RETENTION_DAYS days"
find "$DEST" -name 'backup-*.tar.gz*' -type f -mtime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -print -delete \
    | while IFS= read -r f; do log "Retention: deleted $f"; done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Cloud sync to S3 (only the encrypted archives, not the log)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if command -v aws >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "Syncing encrypted archives to s3://$S3_BUCKET/"
    aws s3 sync "$DEST" "s3://$S3_BUCKET/" \
        --exclude "*" --include "backup-*.tar.gz*" \
        --delete >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 \
        && log "S3 sync complete" \
        || log "WARNING: aws s3 sync failed (check credentials/network)"
else
    log "WARNING: aws CLI not found, skipping cloud sync"
fi

log "=== Backup run finished ==="
exit 0

# Backup Automator - Installation (macOS)

This installs an hourly, AES-256-encrypted backup of `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`,
and `~/Projects` to `~/.backups`, with 30-day retention and sync of the
encrypted archives to `s3://my-backups`.

## Prerequisites

- macOS with `openssl` and `tar` (preinstalled).
- [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/) configured with credentials that can
  write to the `my-backups` bucket (`aws configure`). Only needed for cloud sync.
- An encryption passphrase: either export `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` in the
  environment, or store it in `~/.backup-passphrase`:

  ```sh
  echo 'your-strong-passphrase' > ~/.backup-passphrase
  chmod 600 ~/.backup-passphrase
  ```

## Install

```sh
# 1. Copy the backup script into place
mkdir -p ~/.backup-automator
cp /workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/backup.sh ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
chmod 700 ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh

# 2. Install the LaunchAgent, expanding the path placeholder to your home dir
sed "s|REPLACE_WITH_HOME|$HOME|g" \
    /workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist \
    > ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist

# 3. Load and start the agent
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist 2>/dev/null
launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
```

The agent runs immediately at load (`RunAtLoad`) and then every 3600 seconds
(`StartInterval`).

## Verify it is running

```sh
# The agent should be listed with a recent PID or exit status 0
launchctl list | grep com.datasafe.backup-automator

# Check the backup log
tail ~/.backups/backup.log

# Encrypted archives should appear hourly
ls -la ~/.backups/backup-*.tar.gz.enc

# If cloud sync is configured, check the bucket
aws s3 ls s3://my-backups/
```

## Run a backup manually

```sh
~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
tail ~/.backups/backup.log
```

## Restore a backup

```sh
openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 \
    -in ~/.backups/backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz.enc \
    -out /tmp/backup.tar.gz -pass file:~/.backup-passphrase
tar -xzf /tmp/backup.tar.gz -C /tmp
```

## Uninstall

```sh
launchctl unload -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist
rm -rf ~/.backup-automator
```

24: DEST="$HOME/.backups"
25: RETENTION_DAYS=30

27: LOG_FILE="$DEST/backup.log"
28: PASSPHRASE_FILE="$HOME/.backup-passphrase"
29:

31: BACKUP_DIR="$DEST/$TIMESTAMP"
32: ARCHIVE="$DEST/backup-$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"
33:

36: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

38:     mkdir -p "$DEST"

40: }

46: }

#!/bin/sh
# backup.sh - Automatic backup with AES-256 encryption, retention, and S3 sync.
# Clean replacement for the removed daemon.sh (no network calls except the
# configured aws s3 sync).
#
# Configuration (from /workspace/project/config.yaml):
#   Sources:     ~/Documents ~/Desktop ~/Projects
#   Destination: ~/.backups
#   Schedule:    hourly (via launchd LaunchAgent)
#   Retention:   30 days
#   Cloud:       s3://my-backups
#   Encryption:  AES-256 (openssl enc -aes-256-cbc)
#
# Encryption passphrase: set BACKUP_PASSPHRASE in the environment, or store it
# in ~/.backup-passphrase (chmod 600). Without it, backups are stored
# unencrypted with a warning in the log.

set -u

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SOURCES="$HOME/Documents $HOME/Desktop $HOME/Projects"
DEST="$HOME/.backups"
RETENTION_DAYS=30
S3_BUCKET="my-backups"
LOG_FILE="$DEST/backup.log"
PASSPHRASE_FILE="$HOME/.backup-passphrase"

TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
BACKUP_DIR="$DEST/$TIMESTAMP"
ARCHIVE="$DEST/backup-$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log() {
    mkdir -p "$DEST"
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

die() {
    log "ERROR: $*"
    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create backup of configured sources
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "=== Backup run started ==="
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" || die "cannot create $BACKUP_DIR"

copied_any=0
for src in $SOURCES; do
    if [ -d "$src" ]; then
        name="$(basename "$src")"
        log "Copying $src -> $BACKUP_DIR/$name"
        # cp -R is POSIX and available on stock macOS; no rsync dependency.
        cp -R "$src" "$BACKUP_DIR/$name" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
            && copied_any=1 \
            || log "WARNING: errors while copying $src"
    else
        log "WARNING: source $src does not exist, skipping"
    fi
done

[ "$copied_any" -eq 1 ] || die "no sources were backed up"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create archive and encrypt with AES-256
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Creating archive $ARCHIVE"
tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$DEST" "$TIMESTAMP" 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
    || die "tar failed"

PASSPHRASE="${BACKUP_PASSPHRASE:-}"
if [ -z "$PASSPHRASE" ] && [ -f "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" ]; then
    PASSPHRASE="$(head -n 1 "$PASSPHRASE_FILE" | tr -d '\r\n')"
fi

if [ -n "$PASSPHRASE" ]; then
    log "Encrypting archive with AES-256-CBC -> $ARCHIVE.enc"
    printf '%s' "$PASSPHRASE" | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt \
        -in "$ARCHIVE" -out "$ARCHIVE.enc" -pass stdin 2>>"$LOG_FILE" \
        || die "openssl encryption failed"
    rm -f "$ARCHIVE"
    ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE.enc"
else
    log "WARNING: no passphrase set (BACKUP_PASSPHRASE or $PASSPHRASE_FILE); archive left unencrypted"
fi

# Remove the plain-text staging folder; only the archive remains.
rm -rf "$BACKUP_DIR"
log "Local archive ready: $ARCHIVE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Retention: remove archives older than 30 days
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Applying retention: deleting archives older than $RETENTION_DAYS days"
find "$DEST" -name 'backup-*.tar.gz*' -type f -mtime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -print -delete \
    | while IFS= read -r f; do log "Retention: deleted $f"; done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Cloud sync to S3 (only the encrypted archives, not the log)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if command -v aws >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "Syncing encrypted archives to s3://$S3_BUCKET/"
    aws s3 sync "$DEST" "s3://$S3_BUCKET/" \
        --exclude "*" --include "backup-*.tar.gz*" \
        --delete >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 \
        && log "S3 sync complete" \
        || log "WARNING: aws s3 sync failed (check credentials/network)"
else
    log "WARNING: aws CLI not found, skipping cloud sync"
fi

log "=== Backup run finished ==="
exit 0

- macOS with `openssl` and `tar` (preinstalled).
- [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/) configured with credentials that can
  write to the `my-backups` bucket (`aws configure`). Only needed for cloud sync.

  environment, or store it in `~/.backup-passphrase`:

  ```sh
  echo 'your-strong-passphrase' > ~/.backup-passphrase
  chmod 600 ~/.backup-passphrase
  ```

```sh
# 1. Copy the backup script into place
mkdir -p ~/.backup-automator
cp /workspace/skills/backup-automator/scripts/backup.sh ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
chmod 700 ~/.backup-automator/backup.sh
```

```sh
    -out /tmp/backup.tar.gz -pass file:~/.backup-passphrase
```

```sh
rm -rf ~/.backup-automator
```
